messages:
julia_csm: Quick weekly health check for Slate (reserved pool slate-reserved-pool). Seeing sustained saturation and queue depth spikes through Thu-Fri. Quick summary:
- GPU hours last 7d: 3,420 (up 9% w/w)
- Pool saturation: 92% sustained, peaking 99% at 2025-11-19 16:22 UTC
- Queue depth: median 12, p95 48
- Avg token latency: 310ms, interactive endpoints >1s on spikes
- Error rate: 0.8% baseline, spike to 3.2% Fri 16:18
- Spend delta vs forecast: +27% this week
Can ops triage and propose short-term mitigations? Also want messaging for the account — they pinged about latency and cost.

ops-monitor: Alert: reserve-pool-saturation(slate-reserved-pool) triggered 3x in last 48h. See dashboard: https://dash.redwood/s/s/slt/saturation

mike_ops: saw this overnight. There's a batching/kernel patch rolled 2025-11-17 that changed batch window defaults; it's increasing effective batch sizes for small interactive requests -> higher tail latency during burst. Also a worker restart on Friday caused temporary backlog.

deploy-bot: deploy slate-runtime@v1.4.7 to prod at 2025-11-17T03:12Z (canary). No automated rollback.

ana_cs: Customer reported multiple >1s responses in their UI Friday evening. They flagged that cost spike is more concerning than latency. Asking if we can throttle background reranking jobs or move them to spot capacity.

mike_ops: Short-term plan:
1) roll back batch-window change for slate pool (5m ROLLBACK) -> reduces average batch size for small chat.
2) enable burst-capacity policy for interactive route (adds +2 GPUs) for next 48h.
3) add simple routing rule to offload non-critical rerank jobs to preemptible nodes.
I'll open a PR and a runtime patch.

mike_ops: quick extract I ran:
```
SELECT time_bucket('1h', ts) AS hr, avg(saturation) as sat, max(queue_depth) as qd
FROM reserved_pool_metrics
WHERE pool = 'slate-reserved-pool' AND ts > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY hr ORDER BY hr DESC LIMIT 24;
```
pattern: sustained sat >0.85 for 60+ hours.

julia_csm: Awesome. Can you include expected delta on spend from the burst-capacity + rollback? The customer wants a simple one-paragraph explanation we can send.

mike_ops: Estimated cost impact: rollback alone -> negligible. Burst capacity (2x GPU for 48h) -> ~$4.8k extra. Offloading reranks -> save ~$1.2k over week. Net ~+$3.6k if we enable burst for 48h.

ryan_sales: If we fix latency/cost quickly, renewal is fine. If it lingers past next invoice they'll escalate. Please mark as high-touch until resolved.

ana_cs: I'll draft the customer note: short explanation, what we changed, what they should expect in 2–4 hours, and the cost delta. Will share for review.

mike_ops: PR: https://git.redwood/p/slate/ops/patches/1234 - will run rollback and enable burst in next 20m.

julia_csm: Thanks team. Follow-up sync Friday 09:00 PT. Action items: mike -> rollback + burst; ana -> customer note; ryan -> flag renewal risk if unresolved by billing cycle. :white_check_mark:
